pros: Near-linear time complexity O(V log V) on real-world graphs
Scales to massive networks (millions of nodes, billions of edges)
No prior knowledge of number of communities needed
High-quality partitions with modularity close to theoretical optimum
Simple to implement with clear two-phase structure
Widely tested and validated across disciplines
Multi-level approach captures communities at different resolutions
Memory-efficient: only needs adjacency list and community assignments
cons: Non-deterministic results due to randomized node ordering
May produce internally disconnected communities (fixed in Leiden)
Modularity resolution limit: misses small communities in large graphs
NP-hard underlying problem; heuristic may get stuck in local optima
No guarantee of optimality or approximation ratio
Cannot detect overlapping communities (one node, one community)
Performance degrades on very dense graphs (closer to O(V²))
Results sensitive to initial conditions and iteration order
Modularity function has known limitations (resolution limit)
Community quality may vary significantly across different runs
